what: The tools carrying a --check mode that tools/check.sh does not run with --check, and WHY each one is not. A ratchet, not a target: this list may shrink, and audit_check_gates.py --gate fails when it grows, when it is left standing above what the tree actually shows, or when a row states no reason.
how_to_change_it: Gate the tool in tools/check.sh and re-run --write, or, if it cannot be gated today, write why_not_gated on its row here — --write carries that field forward — and point owner_ticket at whoever owns the answer. The gate fails on a row with no reason, and on a row the gate has since started running.

ungated.why_not_gated: Not gateable per commit: `--check` re-reads the Wright sheet over the IIIF endpoint (the region caches to /tmp and is not committed) and needs numpy and Pillow, so a cold tree reaches the network. Measured GREEN — 5 s, 11 corridors, none drifted more than 0.6 ft — with the readers installed. The way to gate it is trace_river.py's split: an offline `--check-properties` half over the committed metres. It has none yet.

RED — T-1222. It was carried under T-0691 until 2026-09-18, when the owner's ruling landed and that ticket shrank to the card gate; what is left here is the pipeline-ordering question and never was the collisions. `--check` reports 798 file(s) differing, re-measured 2026-09-17. T-0662 read that drift and found byte-identity to be the WRONG CONTRACT for this pass: it is not the last writer of the files it derives. tools/synthesize_resident_research.py rewrites the `letter_list_only` cohort's grade, subtype and note and retires households outright, so re-running the mint over the committed tree REVERTS that work — grades go back from `inferred` to `attested` and the PROJECTED RESIDENT qualifier is stripped from post-office-only names, a confidence upgrade this project forbids — and 54 households are re-minted under changed ids (hh_adains_will_si becomes hh_adains_willisi) out of the same name-splitting fault as the documented mint. Gating it wants a contract that compares what this pass owns, not the whole file. check.sh runs --gate and --self-test, which prove different things.

A spent one-shot. `--check` exits 2 refusing: no household carries a legacy hh_doc_/hh_placed_/hh_ll_ prefix any more, so the migration is done and there is no committed file left for it to re-derive. Retire the mode, or the tool, rather than gate it.

Not gateable per commit, for the reason check.sh already states about trace_river.py: `--check` re-traces a Digital Commonwealth scan over the network and needs numpy, scipy and Pillow. Its three sibling traces carry a `--check-properties` offline half the gate does run; this one does not, and writing it is how this gets gated. Measured GREEN — 24 s, all 316 water vertices and both harbour shore runs stand.

`--check` fetches the leaf images from the archive and needs Pillow, so it cannot be a per-commit gate. check.sh runs `--offline`, which proves a different and gateable thing: that the committed measurement re-derives without the network. Named by T-0896 before it started.

T-0727/T-1156. The --check re-measures the boot payload in a real headless browser against the PUBLISHED mirror (~40 s plus a publish) — check.sh takes seconds and runs no browser. Deliberately ungated until T-1156 wires it into a nightly smoke leg, whose leg budgeting belongs to T-0167.

T-1246. --check boots the published mirror in real Chromium for the device/tier cold/warm timing matrix and 250 ms flora paint heartbeat. check.sh deliberately has no browser dependency; tools/test_boot_phases.mjs gates the deterministic phase/readiness/history contract there. The published browser check and failure/resume cases are run explicitly for this ticket, with the measured receipt in tools/boot_phase_measurements.json. A timing run must use a quiet browser host rather than concurrent per-commit gate jobs.
